ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The demodulator in the attached figure first sends the input x(t) into a multiplier; the other input of the multiplier is labeled cos(2π(fc+40)t). The multiplier output then enters an ideal low-pass filter labeled “Ideal LPF with cut-off 510 Hz”, and the filter amplitude-frequency schematic shows that the passband is from -510 Hz to 510 Hz, with the output terminal labeled y(t). Reasoning: m(t)=4cos(1000πt)=4cos(2π·500t), so x(t)=4cos(2π·500t)cos(2πfc t). Using the product-to-sum formula, x(t)=2cos(2π(fc+500)t)+2cos(2π(fc-500)t). Then multiply again by the local oscillator cos(2π(fc+40)t) in the figure. For the upper sideband 2cos(2π(fc+500)t), after multiplying by the local oscillator, a difference frequency cos(2π·460t) and a high-frequency sum-frequency term are obtained; for the lower sideband 2cos(2π(fc-500)t), after multiplying by the local oscillator, a difference frequency cos(2π·540t) and a high-frequency sum-frequency term are obtained. Therefore the low-frequency part is cos(2π·460t)+cos(2π·540t). The cutoff frequency of the ideal low-pass filter in the figure is 510 Hz, therefore the 460 Hz component passes, while the 540 Hz component and all high-frequency sum-frequency terms are filtered out. Thus y(t)=cos(2π·460t)=cos(920πt).
